scope: Frozen diagnostic private-helper representation, calling-convention, captured-state and redundant-width-check intervention; not a production compiler change or allocation-only ablation.

independent_explanation.workflow: Fresh behavioral explanation without implementation access, parent code inspection, critical debate, and actual Node witnesses.
independent_explanation.conclusion: Accepted after documenting valid-domain width-check invariants and executing the unmodified reassembly control.

index_safety_proof: The top-level sort calls the helper with left=0 and right=vector-length-1. Empty and singleton vectors skip partition because left<right is false.
Every active partition has 0<=left<right<vector-length and a fixed-size non-null array. The original right-width guard remains before the pivot read.
Up starts at left-1 and increments before use. On later partition-loop entries the preceding i<j test implies i<right. It returns within [left,right], reading only while i<right.
Down starts at right and decrements before use. On later loop entries i<j with i>=left implies j>left. It returns within [left,right-1], reading only while j>left.
Both swap indices and all post-crossing reads are in the same valid array. Duplicates/equal values still advance i and decrease j. The array length cannot change.
Recursion uses [left,i-1] and [i+1,right]. An empty child bypasses partition; every active child satisfies the parent bounds. Smaller-first ordering is unchanged.
All read/store indices fit unsigned i32. The initial left-1=-1 is incremented before a read; other arithmetic remains within a vector length and cannot overflow i64.
Every removed repeated width check therefore succeeds on supported calls. Moving the first j-width check before the i-read introduces no earlier trap; original array accesses remain valid.
